description: Collaborative weekly meal planner (AWS course final project). Requirements are frozen in docs/requirements.md; architecture is human-owned and partially pending (docs/architecture.md).

rules.requirements_are_frozen: Never edit docs/requirements.md, app_user_stories.md, coverage_analysis.md, gaps_and_resolutions.md or gaps_pending_stakeholders.md. Every R<n> must cite an existing FR-*/NFR-* id.
rules.architecture_is_human_owned: Never decide anything listed in docs/architecture.md section 2. Set status blocked instead.
rules.never_generate_iac_or_ci: Agents never write Terraform, IaC or CI/CD files. init.sh fails if they appear.

tiers.0: Scaffolding. No product requirement behind it.
tiers.1: Pure domain logic. Architecture-independent — buildable and fully testable today.
tiers.2: Ports and application services. Needs the REST contract decided.
tiers.3: Adapters. Blocked on the corresponding architecture decision.
tiers.4: Frontend. Blocked on the human's initial code drop.
tiers.5: Infrastructure and pipelines. Human-owned, never agent-generated.

features.name: project_scaffold
features.title: Python project scaffold and quality toolchain
features.description: uv workspace backend (core + lambda_api + lambda_ai) plus a separate frontend toolchain root, with pytest, ruff, mypy and pre-commit wired up. No product logic. Layout per docs/architecture.md section 3.
acceptance: backend/pyproject.toml is a uv workspace root ([tool.uv.workspace] members = core, lambda_api, lambda_ai) with shared ruff/mypy/pytest config
backend/core is distribution planner-core with ZERO runtime dependencies; src-layout package planner_core with domain, application, ports subpackages (each with __init__.py)

backend/lambda_api (planner-api) and backend/lambda_ai (planner-ai) each depend on planner-core only (their AWS/AI deps are added later with their adapters, per P1/P4); src-layout packages planner_api and planner_ai exist
ruff configured (format + check, line length 100) and passing across the workspace
mypy configured in strict mode across the workspace, and passing
pytest configured with the 'aws' marker registered and deselected by default (-m 'not aws'); at least one smoke test passing in core/tests
pre-commit config running ruff format, ruff check and mypy on staged files
uv export --package planner-api --no-dev resolves the api closure without the AI SDK (verifies the split is real)
frontend/ exists as its own toolchain root, untouched by the Python gates
./init.sh detects the workspace and runs all four gates green
No Terraform, no CI workflow, and no runtime dependency on core is added

features.name: week_calendar
features.title: ISO week model and Europe/Madrid scoping
features.description: Current/next live week computation as ISO weeks in Europe/Madrid, plus the today-onward scoping rule shared by AI generation and shopping aggregation. Time enters through a Clock port.
acceptance: A Clock port exists in planner_core.ports; no domain code calls datetime.now()
current_week and next_week are computed as ISO weeks (Monday-Sunday) in Europe/Madrid
A week exposes its 7 days and, per day, the lunch and dinner slots
A week exposes its Monday-Sunday date range for UI labelling (FR-UX-06)
A today-onward scoping function returns only slots from the present day forward for the current week, and all slots for the next week
DST transitions and year boundaries are covered by tests
Tests use a fixed FakeClock; no real clock, no network

features.name: text_and_units
features.title: Fixed unit vocabulary and text normalization
features.description: The shared kernel behind ingredient aggregation and cuisine matching: the fixed unit list plus case-, accent- and trim-insensitive normalization.
acceptance: A fixed unit list is defined as a closed vocabulary (concrete values proposed in design.md per G-39)
normalize(name) is case-, accent- and leading/trailing-whitespace-insensitive
Normalization performs no stemming, no singular/plural folding and no synonym matching (G-56 explicitly rejects these)
Tests prove 'Tomate', 'tomate ' and 'tomate' with an accent normalize to one key
A value outside the fixed unit list is rejected with a named domain exception

features.name: recipe_model
features.title: Recipe entity and meal snapshots
features.description: Immutable Recipe with name, ingredients (quantity + unit from the fixed list), tools, procedure, cuisine and difficulty; plus the snapshot taken when a recipe enters a week.
acceptance: Recipe is a frozen dataclass carrying name, ingredients, tools, procedure, cuisine, difficulty
Ingredient quantities only accept units from the fixed unit list (FR-LIB-05)
Difficulty is a closed predefined scale; cuisine is free text normalized for matching (FR-LIB-06)
A snapshot function produces a value object decoupled from the library entry (FR-CAND-07)
Test proves editing or deleting the library recipe leaves an existing snapshot unchanged (G-05)

features.name: week_plan_model
features.title: Candidates, definitive selection and attribution
features.description: Slot contents for a live week: add/edit/remove candidates, promote one to definitive, clear the definitive, duplicate warnings, and author attribution with the unknown-user placeholder.
acceptance: A slot holds a list of candidates and at most one definitive (FR-MENU-03)

A candidate is constructible from any of the three authoring sources - a library recipe pick, a from-scratch recipe, or an accepted AI preview - all landing as the same snapshot-backed candidate (FR-CAND-02, FR-CAND-07)
Promoting a candidate replaces any previous definitive; clearing returns all meals to candidate status (FR-CAND-05, FR-CAND-08)
A promoted meal remains editable; edits propagate wherever it is shown (G-67)
Adding a candidate whose normalized name matches one already in the slot returns a warning but still adds it (FR-CAND-01, G-59)
Saving a meal to the library always creates a new entry and warns on same-name collision (FR-CAND-06, G-26)
Every candidate and every definitive promotion carries its author (FR-CAND-04, FR-SUM-02)
Attribution resolves to the reserved unknown-user placeholder when the author was removed (FR-SUM-03, G-29)

features.name: rules_model
features.title: Shared generation rules and satisfiability
features.description: The dropdown-only shared rule set: ingredient-category counts, pinned library meals per slot, disabled days; plus the constraint solver that prevents contradictory combinations and the per-run override.
acceptance: The three rule types are modelled: category counts, pinned meal per day/slot, disabled days (FR-RULE-04)
The ingredient-category list is a fixed predefined set (concrete values proposed in design.md per G-63)
Available options are constrained so contradictory rule sets cannot be composed: category totals exceeding available slots after disabled days, or a pin on a disabled day (FR-RULE-07)
Deleting a library recipe referenced by a pin rule surfaces a warning and removes the rule on confirmation (FR-RULE-07, G-20)
A per-run override produces an effective rule set without mutating the shared rules (FR-RULE-05, G-06)
Rule edits carry author attribution (FR-RULE-06)

features.name: shopping_aggregation
features.title: Deterministic ingredient aggregation
features.description: Pure function from the in-scope definitive meals to the auto-item set. Matches on normalized name + unit, no cross-unit conversion, idempotent by construction.
acceptance: Aggregation derives only from definitive meals; candidates never contribute (FR-SHOP-05, G-04)
Scope is the current week from today onward plus the whole next week (FR-SHOP-05)
Items merge only on matching normalized name + unit; no cross-unit conversion (FR-SHOP-03)
The function is pure and deterministic: same inputs produce the same auto-item set, so repeated runs converge (FR-SHOP-10, G-54)
Each auto item records which live week(s) require it (needed by rollover cleanup, G-53)
Test proves running the aggregation twice yields an identical result

features.name: shopping_list_state
features.title: Shopping list state, re-sync and check-off
features.description: The shared list: manual vs auto items, manual overrides, check-off, the re-sync merge rules, duplicate flagging, and the quantity-changed-while-checked flag.
acceptance: One shared list; auto items are distinguishable from manual ones (FR-SHOP-01, FR-SHOP-04)
Re-sync updates quantities, adds new items and removes stale UNCHECKED auto items only (FR-SHOP-06)
Manual items, manual overrides and checked items are always preserved by re-sync (FR-SHOP-06, G-21, G-32)
Editing an auto item's name or quantity converts it into a manual override (G-21)
Items are checkable and uncheckable; checked ones sort into a separate section below (FR-SHOP-07, FR-SHOP-08)
A re-sync that changes a checked item's quantity keeps it checked and flags it as updated (FR-SHOP-08, G-44)
Manual and auto items sharing a normalized name + unit both remain but are grouped and marked as likely duplicates (FR-SHOP-11, G-55)

features.name: password_policy
features.title: NIST 800-63B password policy
features.description: Password validation for the mandatory set-password step: length bounds, no composition rules, no rotation, and a blocklist including common Spanish passwords.
acceptance: Minimum length 10, accepted up to at least 64 characters without truncation (FR-AUTH-15)
No mandatory character-composition rules and no forced periodic rotation are enforced (FR-AUTH-15)
A common/breached-password blocklist rejects matches
The blocklist includes common Spanish-language passwords, not only English ones (G-60)
Username validation enforces uniqueness among active accounts and reserves the unknown-user placeholder name (FR-AUTH-17, G-42, G-58)
Rejection messages come from the es-ES messages module (FR-UX-03)

features.name: generation_request
features.title: Generation request, effective rules and idempotency key
features.description: Resolves the effective rule set for a run (shared rules plus optional per-run override), determines target slots, and derives the idempotency key that prevents duplicate candidates and duplicate AI charges.
acceptance: Effective rules = shared rules with the per-run override applied, leaving shared rules untouched (FR-AI-05, FR-RULE-05)
Target slots exclude disabled days; pinned slots resolve to their pinned library meal (FR-AI-11)
For the current week, target slots start at today (Europe/Madrid) — never days already past (FR-AI-11, G-45)
Generation adds candidates and never removes existing candidates or definitives (FR-AI-11, G-18)
An idempotency key is derived from week + slots + effective rules (FR-AI-08)
Test proves the same request submitted twice yields one candidate set and one logical invocation
The three modes (library-only / AI-only / mix) are modelled (FR-AI-03)

features.name: ai_prompt_builder
features.title: AI prompt construction
features.description: Provider-agnostic prompt assembly: Castilian Spanish output, configured servings, category counts as explicit instructions, the fixed unit vocabulary, and the healthy/varied-protein instruction.
acceptance: Prompts are assembled as plain data structures with no provider SDK imported (P4 is still pending)
Every prompt states the configured number of servings (FR-AI-13, G-64)
Every prompt instructs Castilian Spanish output (FR-AI-07)
Every prompt instructs healthy, balanced menus that vary protein sources, labelled non-medical (FR-AI-06)
Ingredient-category counts are passed as explicit prompt instructions, honored best-effort (FR-AI-04, G-63)
Prompts constrain ingredient units to the fixed unit list (FR-LIB-05, G-48)
Both single-recipe modes are supported: from specifications, and from a library reference plus specifications (FR-AI-01, FR-AI-02)

features.name: ai_output_validation
features.title: AI output validation and preview lifecycle
features.description: Validates model output against the recipe schema and the fixed unit list, and models the accept/discard/regenerate preview plus per-slot failure results.
acceptance: Output failing the recipe schema or using a unit outside the fixed list is rejected, not silently accepted (G-48)
Single-recipe generation produces a preview that can be accepted, discarded or regenerated; nothing persists until accepted (FR-AI-10, G-17)
Regenerations count toward the generation caps (FR-AI-10, NFR-AI-01)
Per-slot results are independent: one slot failing does not abort the others and partial results are kept (FR-AI-09, FR-AI-12)
Insufficient library recipes for library-only or mix mode produces an explicit named failure, never a silent partial result (FR-AI-12, G-66)
Failure messages come from the es-ES messages module (FR-UX-03)

features.name: rollover_job_logic
features.title: Week rollover as an idempotent state transition
features.description: The five-step rollover expressed as a pure, re-runnable transition: archive the ending week, snapshot the shopping list, promote next to current, initialize a new empty next week, clean bought items.
acceptance: The five steps execute in order: archive, shopping-list snapshot, promote next to current, init empty next week, clean bought items (FR-MENU-06, G-61)
The archive snapshot is taken BEFORE the cleanup (FR-ARCH-02, G-53)
The former next week becomes the current week carrying over its candidates and definitives (FR-MENU-06, G-28)
The new next week starts empty; rules never auto-populate it (FR-MENU-06, G-15)
Cleanup removes CHECKED items unless still required by the new current week; unchecked items are untouched (FR-SHOP-09, G-53)
Archived weeks become read-only (FR-ARCH-02)
Test proves re-running after interruption at each of the five steps completes without data loss, double-archiving or double-cleanup (FR-MENU-08, G-61)

features.name: persistence_ports
features.title: Persistence ports and in-memory adapters
features.description: Repository interfaces for accounts, recipes, weeks, rules, the shopping list and the archive, plus in-memory fakes and the contract-test harness that will later run against the real adapter.
acceptance: Ports are typing.Protocol definitions in planner_core.ports with no storage technology leaking into their signatures
In-memory fakes in core/tests/support implement every port and are used by application-layer tests
A contract suite in backend/tests/contract exercises each port and is parametrized to run against any implementation (fake now, real adapter later)
No AWS SDK import anywhere in this feature
features.blocked_reason: Architecture P1 (datastore) undecided. Port shapes depend on whether access is key-value or relational — see docs/architecture.md section 2.

features.name: auth_flow
features.title: Authentication, sessions and account lifecycle
features.description: Login, the mandatory set-password step, temporary admin-assigned passwords, session lifetimes, session invalidation, admin account management and user removal.
acceptance: Deferred until the auth mechanism is chosen
features.blocked_reason: Architecture P2 (auth mechanism) undecided. A managed identity provider would supply forced password change, session invalidation and brute-force protection natively; an application-managed design must build all three.

features.name: rest_api_lambda
features.title: REST API Lambda
features.description: The api Lambda: routing, request validation, domain exception to error mapping, and wiring of application use cases.
acceptance: Deferred until the REST contract is defined
features.blocked_reason: Architecture P5 (REST API contract) and P6 (deployment topology) undecided.

features.name: ai_lambda
features.title: AI generation Lambda
features.description: The ai Lambda: provider client, per-slot concurrency, idempotent invocation, cost cap enforcement.
acceptance: Deferred until the AI provider is chosen
features.blocked_reason: Architecture P4 (AI provider and model) undecided. The per-user daily generation cap is derived from the 50 EUR/month budget and provider pricing (G-38).

features.name: realtime_channel
features.title: Real-time collaboration channel
features.description: Broadcasting changes to both live weeks, the shopping list, the rules and the library; connection-loss indication, automatic reconnect and state re-synchronization.
acceptance: Deferred until the real-time transport is chosen

features.name: archive_and_cold_storage
features.title: Archive browsing and cold-storage lifecycle
features.description: Reverse-chronological archive navigation, indefinite retention, and the scheduled job moving records older than ~3 months to cold storage with a restoring state in the UI.
acceptance: Deferred until the datastore and cold-storage wiring are chosen
features.blocked_reason: Architecture P1 (datastore) and P6 (cold-storage wiring) undecided.

features.name: frontend_spa
features.title: Single-page application
features.description: The responsive es-ES SPA: two live weeks, candidates and the three-way authoring flow (library pick / from scratch / AI, reused by library authoring minus the self-pick), definitive selection, library, rules, shopping list, summary and archive.
acceptance: Deferred until the initial frontend code is supplied
features.blocked_reason: Waiting on the human's initial frontend code (architecture P7: framework identity, bootstrap idiom, test runner) and on feature 16, since the SPA needs the REST contract. The frontend stack and conventions are already specified - see docs/conventions.md section 'Frontend conventions'.

The architecture-decision section reflects the human's actual decisions, not agent speculation
